p.d: Inman and Eddins assist on a manhunt when a suspect runs a constable off the road in southeast Texas. Meanwhile, a landlord complains about trespassers
Dr Jeff treats a skittish Savannah cat with an unusual condition. Thee team races to save a stray dog as it runs toward the motorway
The team cares for abandoned kittens. Plus, Dr Jeff gives hope to a concerned owner when their beloved dog is diagnosed with cancer, and a rescue tiger finds love
A stray dog found under a home turns out to be terrified of humans. A couple who have visited Villalobos before want to adopt a dog that is comfortable on a boat
Lizzy and Elise struggle to rescue a dangerously dehydrated dog. An abandoned and anxious pooch is moved to a new warehouse for canines with special needs
Behaviourist Jackson Galaxy examines the psychological patterns of feline Dexter, who has developed a killing streak. Plus a cat given as a birthday present proves a bad omen
Behaviourist Jackson Galaxy helps Greg and Dina, who are worried about their vicious cat. Plus, Chris and Tenille baulk at moving in together because of the latter's hostile feline
Pete Nelson and his gang ride out to build a double-decker hideout in Texas Hill Country, featuring a saloon-style first floor
Footage of animals, featuring a balloon-popping bulldog who thinks everything belongs to her and a cat that steals from everyone in its neighbourhood
High-speed footage reveals how the hummingbird can fly backwards, and a look at the hagfish, which is unlikely to win any underwater beauty contests
What a dog is saying when it wags its tail, and the secret behind a crocodile's powerful jaws - and how to escape it

Documentary following teams coming to the aid of distressed or missing felines. Shaun heads out on a solo night mission to rescue an animal that has been missing three weeks, and joins Tom in an attempt to rescue a feral cat
Shaun and Tom investigate whether a stranded cat is really who its owner says it is. There is also an attempt to reunite a feline with its canine companion
An in-depth interview with Noah Brown, the clan's 'Mr Fix-It'
A California restaurant is looking for a tank for their new location in Santa Monica. The owners want a nostalgic feel and replicas to represent the restaurant's history

England v Pakistan. Highlights of day five of the Third and Final Test in the series from Edgbaston in Birmingham. The teams had not met in a Test at this venue since 2016, when England prevailed by 141 runs, and the hosts have won four and lost four of the eight matches played in this format here since

Highlights from a summer of extraordinary music at the world's biggest classical music festival. From Berlioz to Beethoven, Miles Davis to Marvin Gaye, this is a special selection of the best musical moments from across the season, including performances by Sheku Kanneh-Mason, Jess Gillam, Ladysmith Black Mambazo and more. Presented by Petroc Trelawny, Georgia Mann, Katie Derham, Nick Mohammed, Andi Oliver and Clive Myrie

The performance artist looks back at the 2021 adaptation of her dramatic monologue, revealing the changes needed to create something for TV that retained the power of the stage play. She discusses the influences behind the show, the need to engage the audience as part of the ritual and the consequences of performing something so physically and emotionally draining

Performance artist Selina Thompson re-creates her award-winning and deeply personal monologue about her journey by cargo ship, retracing the route of the transatlantic slave trade. Throughout the film, Thompson explores her painfully difficult but ultimately redemptive exploration of the Atlantic triangle in a cathartic pilgrimage through grief, race and identity

p.t: Stephen Tompkinson Remembers - The Deep Blue Sea
p.d: The actor looks back on his role in the BBC's 1994 adaptation of the acclaimed Terence Rattigan play, directed by pioneer of British film Karel Reisz and also starring Colin Firth, Ian Holm and Penelope Wilton. He explains why he seized the opportunity to join the cast, recalls the challenges involved and describes in particular what it was like to witness in person Penelope Wilton's central performance as Hester, described by critics as one of the decade's greatest acting masterclasses

Hester is rescued by a neighbour after attempting suicide in the flat she shares with her younger lover, ex-RAF pilot Freddie Page. Karel Reisz's 1994 adaptation of Terence Rattigan's play, starring Penelope Wilton, Colin Firth, Ian Holm, Stephen Tompkinson, Geraldine Somerville and Carmel McSharry

p.t: Nature and Us: A History Through Art
p.d: James Fox considers the way art over the past 100 years reflects how nature was swapped for progress in the first half of the 20th century, before rediscovering its beauty in the decades following the Second World War, and how today's artists are reimagining the human race's future relationship with nature

A guide to life on the footplate of the nation's favourite steam engine. Cameras are placed aboard locomotive 60103 as it travels along the Severn Valley, cutting through stunning landscapes on a journey from Bridgnorth to Kidderminster. The 'cab cameras' capture veteran driver Roger Norfolk and fireman Ryan Green in action as they talk through the mechanics and challenges of operating this national treasure. Needless to say, things sometimes get hot on the footplate and not everything goes exactly to plan

Part two of two. The naturalist reaches the peak of one of Venezuela's tepui mountains, before joining a party of Italian cavers as they venture into the unexplored caverns within. Inside, they discover strange wildlife and evidence of the geological forces that give the tepuis their unusual shape. Finally, the team returns to the ground by abseiling down the Angel Falls, the world's highest waterfall

The last in a set of four documentaries exploring wildlife and plants throughout the year focuses on the spring, when hibernating animals awake and many species search for mates. The programme features footage of grizzly bear cubs, the mating dances of grebes, flowers growing in the desert and swifts embarking on marathon journeys

Bendor Grosvenor and Emma Dabiri visit Brighton Museum to investigate who painted two neglected pictures of religious subjects. Plus, Emma investigates how Brighton's Royal Pavilion ended up an empty shell, ransacked and sold to the local council
Magnus Magnusson hosts the sixth heat of the quiz, with four contenders answering questions on the specialist subjects of George Orwell, the history of costume from 1600, Rome, and the Common Market
Robert Robinson presides over another duel of words and wits as Diana Quick, Robert Powell, Anouska Hempel and Nigel Havers join captains Frank Muir and Patrick Campbell. First broadcast in 1979

Live coverage of the half-marathon, which sees more than 60,000 runners of all abilities negotiate the course from Newcastle upon Tyne to South Shields. Kenya's Alex Mutiso took the honours in the men's race last year, and his compatriot Sheila Chepkirui was victorious in the women's event

A look ahead to the latest forecast
Mark Carruthers looks at the political developments of the week and questions policy makers on the key issues
Aled Jones marks 500 years since William Tyndale's translation of the New Testament into English, exploring its radical impact and meeting those continuing his mission

Izzie Balmer and Saf Fakir meet globetrotter Jenny who has been given the daunting task of clearing the family home since her mum has moved to an end-of-life care facility. She's decided any auction proceeds will fund an art exhibition showcasing her late grandmother's paintings. Izzie unearths forgotten treasures including a rare book and valuable jewellery and Saf transforms an old blanket box to sell

Lolly Spence meets the owner of a vintage steamer trunk used during the golden age of transatlantic travel. After years of use and abuse, the trunk has seen better days, and restoring it back to working order won't be easy
In autumn, preparations for the winter begin and the lough becomes busy with grey seal pups and thousands of geese
A round-up of the latest headlines
The latest forecast

Coverage of the third and final day of the inaugural staging of the biennial track and field invitational event, which takes place at the National Athletics Centre in Budapest, Hungary. The men's 400m hurdles is likely to feature a showdown between world and Olympic champion Rai Benjamin of USA and Brazilian Alison dos Santos, who recently broke the world record. A packed schedule also sees titles handed out in the women's 400m hurdles, 5,000m, triple jump and 200m, the men's javelin, high jump, 800m, 1500m and 200m, and the mixed 4x400m relay

Fiona Bruce presents from Dartington Estate in Devon, where finds include shoes modelled to look like feet and a quirky ceramic model of a Cavalier King Charles Spaniel. Fiona also gets a glimpse of rare historic clothing from a collection housed at nearby Falmouth University, including a Georgian dress and a side saddle horse riding costume from the 1920s, and takes up Chris Yeo's challenge to place three pieces of Devon studio pottery in order of value.

The truth of Jia's discovery has dangerous consequences for the team, who have to band together to go on a rescue mission that could spell disaster. As enemies both old and new draw nearer in pursuit of the real prize, loyalties are tested and shocking revelations made
A round-up of today's headlines
On the day of Cindy and Max, and Kim and Howie's weddings, Zoe encourages Tommy to open up
Chaos erupts at Max and Cindy's wedding, and Denise receives positive news
The fallout of Max and Cindy's wedding continues, the Slaters are angry at Zoe's actions, while Ned and Gemma try to acquaint themselves with the residents of Walford
Emotions remain at an all-time-high in Walford, and Alfie encourages Kat to make amends with Zoe

Action from the half-marathon, which took place on a course from Newcastle upon Tyne to South Shields. The men's course record was set at 58:56 in 2011 by Kenya's Martin Mathathi, and his compatriot Brigid Kosgei holds the women's mark, having run 1:04:28 in 2019

Belfast police probationer Grace tries to help a fellow single mother whose son has fallen in with a notorious gang. However, fulfilling her promise could put her at risk from both sides of the law. Her fellow new recruits Annie and Tommy deal with an apprehensive colleague and undercover agents at work in the city, while their superior officer finds himself being threatened by MI5. Drama following three new recruits to Belfast's police force, starring Siân Brooke

The team scrambles to deal with a series of mysterious emergencies across the city, all stemming from a bad batch of drugs. The McIntyre gang soon realise the crisis can be traced back to one of their young drug runners, has been selling drugs outside of their area, so race to cover their tracks. Annie receives terrifying news that has her wondering who she can trust even within her own community

After African American photographer Chris and his white girlfriend Rose visit her wealthy parents, he suspects there's more to the locals than meets the eye. Oscar-winning psychological thriller written and directed by Jordan Peele (Us), starring Daniel Kaluuya, Allison Williams, Bradley Whitford and Caleb Landry Jones

Nate and Mobeen are just weeks from the end of their sentence, but Mobeen's work as one of the prison's 'listeners' gets him into trouble with a terrifying inmate from another wing, a man known simply as Megalodon. While contending with this problem, Mobeen receives a visit from Aqsa, who's getting frustrated with certain aspects of life at medical school. Comedy, starring Guz Khan and Tolu Ogunmefun

In the prison infirmary, Mobeen sets out to befriend a man known as Memory Stick and convince him to hand over vital information. He also encounters a doctor, Nida, and there's an instant spark between the two of them. While Mobeen's in the hospital, Nate and Officer Harper develop a 'bromance'. Comedy, starring Guz Khan and Tolu Ogunmefun

Despite the danger that leaving the cell puts him in, Mobeen heads to see Jamal in response to a call for help - only to encounter Megalodon on the way. Just when it looks like Megalodon is about to batter Mobeen, Officer Saj intervenes, leaving Mobeen free to help Jamal, which he does with help from an unlikely source. Comedy, starring Guz Khan and Youssef Kerkour

Megalodon throws the prison into a full-blown riot. Mobeen, Nate and Harper split off into different groups. Mobeen is concerned with Dr Nida's safety, while also trying to keep Memory Stick on side. Uncle Shady ends up with Memory Stick, with both of them trying to evade Megalodon and a wing full of rioting inmates. However, as the Tornado Team arrives, Mobeen ends up in the climactic showdown in which a number of revelations emerge. Comedy, starring Guz Khan and Youssef Kerkour

p.t: Roman Kemp: The Fight for Young Lives
p.d: Broadcaster Roman Kemp knows first-hand the impact of serious mental health issues. In 2020, he made Our Silent Emergency in the wake of the death of a friend. He encouraged those in need to talk to friends, family and professionals, but now strives to move the conversation on from talking about mental health to discovering what action is needed to support those suffering

On a Bradford estate, Lenny and Mullet find an abandoned car and turn it into a DIY spaceship. Elif Riley, Logan Ludbrook, Lucy Francis and Hayley Brown star in this kitchen-sink sci-fi comedy about big dreams, everyday lives and escaping without going anywhere
Matt Tebbutt presents more highlights, with recipes by Elliott Grover, Theo Randall and Tony Singh, while Romesh Ranganathan tucks into either his food heaven or hell

In Glasgow, Levi Roots tempts shoppers with an aromatic pineapple dessert, before taking to the seas to meet Mull fishermen. He also lays on the ultimate Caribbean cricket tea for two teams of hungry Yorkshiremen

p.t: Lorraine Pascale: How to Be a Better Cook
p.d: Sonia Harwood is a mother-of-three and foster carer who would love to create homemade family meals, but ends up relying on frozen food. Lorraine shows her how easy it can be to cook with fresh ingredients, preparing dishes including courgette fritters, a quick seafood linguine and a baked ricotta cheesecake
Anita Manning is joined by Nick Hall and Danny Sebastian at Mona Showground on Anglesey, and pays a visit to a local jewellery maker to find out more about amber

p.t: The Big Deal with Steph McGovern
p.d: Steph welcomes the budding art dealers on board the luxurious Queen Anne cruise liner for the semi-final. Their three-day task sees them curating a collection of art fit for the ship's new cabaret bar. The operators have pledged to buy one collection up to the value of £35,000 from the winners, who will earn 20 per cent commission. But not everyone will be so lucky and it is up to Cordelia de Freitas and guest mentors Wilhelm Finger and Melita Skamnaki to decide who should leave

Arsenal v Crystal Palace (Kick-off 2.45pm). All the action from the match at Emirates Stadium. The Gunners finished second behind Manchester City last term and will be looking to go one better this time around after signing the likes of Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Selina Cerci. They take on a Palace side who bounced back to the top flight at the first time of asking after finishing as runners-up in WSL2 last season

Paul Martin and the team examine antiques at Ashridge House, Hertfordshire. Thomas Plant discovers a marble cupid statue while a 19th-century brass microscope with an extensive collection of botanical slides catches the eye of Claire Rawle. Plus, the presenter takes time out to explore art at the Henry Moore Foundation in Much Hadham, which houses the largest collection of Moore's work

Eagles are the most powerful birds in the sky, capable of tackling enormous prey, spotting food at vast distances and soaring for miles on the wing. Armed with cutting-edge filming technology, this documentary examines the science behind such extraordinary abilities. Featuring dramatic stories and some remarkable experiments, the film follows the story of a family of bald eagles in Iowa as two chicks face the challenges of life in the wild. Plus, bird specialist Lloyd Buck puts his trained golden eagle Tilly's skills to the test

Joe Crowley, Datshiane Navanayagam and Adam Henson head to Westacre Estate in Norfolk to discover how a historic rural estate is adapting to survive in the modern world. At a financially critical time of year, Datshiane looks at its valuable yet vulnerable crop of blueberries and meets the owner to find out how traditional estates are diversifying and evolving to secure their future. Joe joins the conservation team working to restore an important area of wet woodland, boosting biodiversity and creating habitats for wildlife, and also visits a tenant brewery and lends a hand to craft a local ale. Meanwhile, Adam meets the farm manager, who is looking at ways to help run the land in a more cost-effective way through collaboration between livestock and arable farming

The pilgrims travel from Appenzell to their final destination at Einsiedeln Abbey. They witness a lively cattle show in Urnasch, learn about the Jewish heritage of two Swiss villages and tackle a muddy and steep path through the mountains as the weather deteriorates further. Finally, they reach the beautiful 10th-century abbey church, with its famed Black Madonna in the Chapel of Mercy

p.t: Rob and Rylan's Passage to India
p.d: Rob Rinder and Rylan Clark go on the final leg of their Indian adventure, beginning by visiting the erotic temples of Khajuraho, ancient structures covered in carvings depicting all kinds of carnal pleasure. In Varanasi, they drift down the sacred Ganges, witnessing pilgrims chasing liberation from reincarnation, before joining a mud-wrestling club inspired by Hanuman, the monkey god of strength
The veteran rock band headline the final day of the event at City Park in Stirling, bringing proceedings to a close with a selection of their hits from across nearly 50 years

Jo Whiley, Sara Cox, Edith Bowman, Vernon Kay and Tina Daheley present performances from the concluding day of the festival at City Park in Stirling, with a line-up featuring Level 42, James Blunt, Blue, Cast, Appleton and Deacon Blue

John Craven and Anita Rani are in Cumbria to see how arable farmers, more used to rain than drought, have fared after a record-breaking dry summer. John also joins Matt Baker in kicking off this year's Countryfile Ramble for BBC Children in Need, while in the Cotswolds, Adam Henson sees how the hot weather has affected his livestock

Documentary following two brothers searching for treasure on a Nova Scotia island. Alex and Jack share insights into the methods they used and the evidence they uncovered

Strictly Come Dancing star Anton Du Beke takes on one of the show's former judges, Arlene Phillips, in a search for potentially profitable antiques. Beginning in West Yorkshire, their route takes in a traditional clog-making business and a trip to Blackpool Tower, before finishing at an auction in Liverpool. Quiz hosted by Bradley Walsh in which six contestants battle it out across a series of fast-paced question rounds where the players must actively try to sabotage their opponents by beating them to the buzzer and trapping them out of the game. Tim Lovejoy and Simon Rimmer are joined by guests Beverley Knight, Lara Pulver, Penn Jillette, Jay Sean and Xand van Tulleken. With music from Bloc Party

While renovating a new bridal bedroom, Julia battles cracked plaster and expensive surprises. Anna and Edward get creative with the candles left over from weddings in a bid to save money. Over at Chateau Gioux, Debbie and Nigel bring new life to an old piano by creating a vibrant gin bar
The competition begins with Nick and Tim at Home Farm B&B in Milton Keynes, where secrets get revealed during a visit to the home of Second World War code breakers

The week's second visit takes the B&Bers to Cricklade in Wiltshire, where Iain and Tayla host at The Vale Hotel. Their breakfast-free, no frills ethos has some of the guests worried, but it's the proximity to a main road that causes the most concern for one pair. Over drinks, the gang try an intimacy exercise that leaves Tayla in an awkward position, before the noisy neighbourhood is cause for much consternation in the feedback

Francesca and Maurizio host the week's third visit at Cottage Lodge Hotel in Brockenhurst in The New Forest. The pair have a background in high-end hotels, and their green approach to hospitality leaves some of the B&Bers impressed but a tree hugging trip divides the group in the afternoon. The hosts' passion for local produce takes pride of place at breakfast but they're left with a sour taste over their facilities scores

Husband-and-wife team Karl and Rohini host the week's final visit, at Beach Sun Retreat in Dymchurch, Kent. Their unusual offering proves an acquired taste for some, as not everyone finds the onsite meditation experience as relaxing as intended. Drinks on the pair's indoor beach brightens the mood, but some are left feeling less enlightened by the veggie breakfast the next morning
It's payment day and the B&Bers take each other to task about some dodgy comments made throughout the week, before the payments are revealed and the winners crowned

p.d: A major snowfall brings stunning landscapes and carefree play days for the kids, while builder Richard is hard at work fitting floors, pipes and electrics. Amanda's off-roader gets stuck in a snowdrift and needs a helping hand from Miles and his tractor, and the family battle members to protect their pregnant sheep scattered across the Fells

p.t: Walkers Unpacked: Inside the Crisp Factory
p.d: Behind the scenes at the Walkers factory as the company launches its crisp flavour and new packaging. The documentary follows the entire process - from farm to test kitchen and the production line, where those on quality control keep an eye out the tiniest of flaws, while others maintain the top-secret machinery and the flavour scientists work hard to find the perfect taste

p.d: Liza Tarbuck hosts a celebrity edition of the pottery challenge, with Lucy Beaumont, Fatiha El-Ghorri, Richard Herring, Paul Merson, Denise Van Outen and Layton Williams. Gordon Ramsay concludes his two-part challenge at Mangia Mangia in Woodland Park, Colorado. In order to save the struggling Italian restaurant from disaster, he must persuade harassed owner Julie to co-operate with the head chef, and work his magic on a menu that relies heavily on a microwave

Teenager Charlie discovers his frequently absent father is secretly a superhero after finding the hi-tech headquarters under his home. However, when an evil mastermind hatches a plot, it falls to Charlie and his friends to use the lair's resources to save the day. Comedy adventure, starring Owen Wilson and Michael Pena

Blue-collar caveman Fred Flintstone is promoted to an executive position at work and unwittingly becomes embroiled in an embezzlement scheme - thanks in no small part to his seductive new assistant. Live-action version of the cartoon comedy, starring John Goodman, Rick Moranis, Rosie O'Donnell, Halle Berry and Elizabeth Taylor

Homer takes Ned Flanders' advice and starts praying regularly, hoping God will lend a sympathetic ear and make it possible for him to buy a better home. Marge warns that his materialistic attitude may incur divine retribution, but he turns a deaf ear - until a flood of biblical proportions hits Springfield

Bart learns that he was once a child celebrity, but that Homer spent all the money he made, so he separates from his parents and moves into a loft apartment, where his neighbours are punk band Blink-182 and skateboarding hero Tony Hawk

Marge offers to babysit Ned Flanders' boys so he can attend a left-handers' convention. Meanwhile, Homer takes the Simpson children to an animal retirement home - where Bart has the misfortune to be kidnapped by a lonely chimpanzee

In an episode written by Ricky Gervais, who provides the voice of a would-be ladies' man, Homer's obsession with Lenny's new plasma TV leaves him desperate to buy one of his own, so he signs up for a wife-swapping show to win the money. Unfortunately, Marge's new 'husband' soon develops a crush on her

Mr Burns sends Homer to train new workers in India, where he is worshipped and granted control of the plant. Meanwhile, Patty and Selma kidnap McGyver star Richard Dean Anderson - who provides his own voice - from a Stargate SG-1 convention to teach him a lesson

When plans for an outing to the Frying Dutchman are ruined, the family tries to salvage the night by recounting three stories about disasters at sea. One of the tales told is about a fugitive called Homer who delivered the Mayflower safely to the New World

A scandal results in Principal Skinner being replaced by a woman who divides the school in half according to gender, so Lisa poses as a boy to attend maths classes. However, it is not long before she comes to the attention of Bart - who sees through her disguise. With the voice of Frances McDormand

With another elimination looming, this next challenge is a tale of two worlds: history above, and mystery below. The nine remaining teams have nine hours to build an above-and-below design, on top of and inside a fishtank, based on different historical eras of civilisation (from Romans to Vikings, and from pirates to cowboys), with a creature lurking beneath. The catch? Once their time is up, the tanks will be filled with water - and the builds must stay intact when submerged. Which duo are out of their depth and will be sent home?

Sparks fly when Gordon visits Blue Island brunch spot Love on the Blu, where there's no love lost between shouty boss lady Valencia and her struggling staff. Can some tough love from Gordon convince Valencia to confront the changes needed to save her business and her team?

A streetwise teenager is taken under the wing of his dead father's old colleague, an agent working for a super-secret spy organisation. Will the youngster turn out to be a chip off the old block by proving useful during a battle against a twisted, hi-tech genius? Action comedy based on a comic book, starring Colin Firth, Taron Egerton and Samuel L Jackson

The armchair critics share their opinions on Oprah with Meghan and Harry and the subsequent news that Piers Morgan had resigned as co-host of Good Morning Britain. Other programmes being considered include Paranormal Lockdown UK, The Celebrity Circle for Stand Up to Cancer, Teen First Dates, Amazing Hotels: Life Beyond the Lobby and BBC News coverage of NHS pay

Anna Richardson is joined by 25 year-old Lauren, a movie buff and professional online gamer from Camberley who is looking for a geeky gamer to be her perfect player two so she can reboot her love life after three years of being single. Ryan who is 28 and from Cheltenham, is looking for his Mr Right. As a sucker for a silver fox and a dad bod, can he find his dream guy to wake up to every morning?

The chef prepares cheese with roast figs and prosciutto, and a classic Greek salad
The chef prepares smoked trout salad and hot tea-smoked trout with celeriac remoulade. He also tries his hand at fly fishing for trout on the River Test in Hampshire
The chef prepares penne carbonara, smoked haddock risotto, and tiramisu, before talking to his regular supplier about classic Italian ingredients
The chef goes looking for wild mushrooms in the New Forest and prepares chilli mushrooms, pasta with cepes sauce and a coffee mushroom dessert

Judges Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood set the remaining contestants three tasks involving pastry, beginning by asking them to make signature suet puddings. For Mary's technical challenge, they must prepare eight religieuse - delicate choux buns filled with creme patissiere and topped with ganache - before creating three different types of perfectly puffed pastries in the showstopper round. Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins present

It's the quarter-final and Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood test how the five remaining contestants cope with unconventional flours and unusual desserts, beginning by baking a signature loaf using non-traditional flours such as spelt, rye, potato and tapioca. In the technical challenge they each have to prepare a gluten-free dacquoise, which is made with meringue, coffee custard and hazelnut praline, before creating dairy-free novelty vegetable cakes for the showstopper round. Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins present

The four semi-finalists face three French challenges, beginning by preparing three types of savoury canapes in just two-and-a-half hours. In the technical challenge they each have to make a Charlotte Royale, a dessert made with Swiss roll and creme bavaroise, before the showstopper round sees them bake opera cakes, which consist of layers of almond sponge with coffee buttercream filling and a chocolate topping. Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins present

Contestants from last year's series talk about their experiences of life inside the tent. They reveal how they coped with having ingredients stolen by Mel and Sue, how practising the art of making bagels, petit fours, meringues, hidden design cakes and gingerbread constructions dominated their lives and what it was really like to work in extreme weather conditions

Twelve contestants battle it out to be named best amateur baker of 2014, beginning by tackling a Swiss roll, a cherry cake and miniature British classics. Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins present and judges Mary Berry and Paul Hollywood cast a critical eye over the contenders' efforts

Having shown they have what it takes to bake a cake or two, the 11 remaining contestants turn their attention to biscuits. First up they create their signature savoury crackers for cheese, and are encouraged to push the flavour. In the technical challenge, they have to prepare Mary Berry's Florentines, with their chewy caramel sauce and brandy-snap texture, before ending with a showstopper like no other - three-dimensional scenes made entirely from biscuits. For one hopeful, there will be the pride of being crowned Star Baker, while another will be sent home - well aware that that's just the way the cookie crumbles. Hosted by Mel Giedroyc and Sue Perkins
A case that began when NYPD officers found a bullet-pierced body found in the boot of a car. Detectives were led into a dark tale of brotherhood, backstabbing and betrayal
A case in which a homeowner was found dead in a driveway, riddled with bullets. The claims of a family member who allegedly witnessed the attack raised more questions than answers
A case in which a 19-year-old went goes missing after going to a party. Her remains were found in a field 15 months later, leaving officers perplexed as to determining a motive

Two women who headed out into the night, full of youthful life and promise, but never came back. Clues came from behind bars to solve the mysteries that surrounded the disturbing disappearances of the duo
The case of a promising young athlete, found shot to death. His family began a relentless hunt for justice
A case in which the remains of a 26-year-old woman were found inside a washer-dryer. The murder shook her community, whose members sought answers to the heinous crime

The case of killer Timothy Bass, who for decades had told his wife Gina that he enjoyed working the night shift to make extra money. Gina believed him until she uncovered his secret and was left wondering what evil her husband had done

It never occurred to Shirley Gaskins that the father she adored could be one of the most prolific serial killers in America. However, the more people vanished without explanation, the harder it was to deny
How a woman faced the hellish truth about her troublemaking son when he committed a monstrous crime. How much could a mother's love for her son withstand?

The case of Steven Crittenden, who in 1987 murdered William and Katherine Chiapella during a home invasion. When he confessed to his half-brother, Bryant Jones, and then swore him to secrecy, Bryant faced the toughest decision of his life - whether to keep the secret and risk letting a murderer get away with it, or tell the truth and betray his family

In 2012, biker and single father Brandon Duran's body was found at the bottom of a pond, covered in concrete. A custody battle between him and former spouse Amber Andrews was found to be the reason of the fatal assault
Terri Lemoine and Sean Vincent Gillis lived a quiet life for 10 years, until it was revealed Gillis was living a double life as a serial killer
A dancer disappears and her torso washes ashore, forcing detectives to chase a killer through New Orleans' dark and dangerous underworld
When an Army veteran vanishes from her apartment, investigators devise a unique surveillance strategy to find her. They uncover disturbing evidence.
CSI Alina Burroughs digs into the murder of Kim Ancona. Alina re-opens the case to find out whether a bite mark is enough to prove murder

A team of five from Nottingham answer Top 10 list questions and attempt to top the Tenable Tower to win £125,000 in the quiz show hosted by Warwick Davis.

They must work as a team and play strategically to answer general knowledge questions against the clock and race down the game board to the exit without being caught

Ranvir Singh hosts the quiz where contestants take on Riddlemaster Henry Lewis in an attempt to solve a series of riddles - packed with themed general knowledge questions and confusing conundrums, only one team can make it through to the high-stakes final with a chance to win an exciting cash prize. How will Faisal and Daniel, Sara and Kaitlin, and Vicki and Richard cope under pressure?

Paralympian Denise and her dog Sherpa aim to become 100,000-pound winners by opening the iconic red boxes. Will the pair take home a fortune, or will the Banker convince Denise to sell her box for a bargain? Join Stephen Mulhern to find out

The fast-paced game of words, hosted by Adil Ray, where three pairs of contestants face Lingo grids, fiendish puzzlewords, and a tense head-to-head round as they battle to reach the final and a chance to win a 15,000-pound jackpot. Taking part alongside the reigning champions are nan and granddaughter Diane and Becky, and mother and son Liz and Adam

G'Kar tries to avoid capture by the Centauri while continuing his search for Garibaldi. Delenn urges the Rangers to strike against the Shadows, while Sheridan hovers between life and death

Ivanova and Marcus search for more First Ones to help in the war, and G'Kar is told to swallow his pride to become more appealing to Cartagia. Meanwhile, a mysterious spacecraft makes its way toward Babylon 5

A corrupt senator coaxes Colonel Custer out of retirement with the prospect of presidential office, and the soldier tries to further his political ambitions by wresting control of the current military campaign from its commanding officer, culminating in his last stand at the Battle of the Little Bighorn. Western, with Philip Carey, Joseph Cotten, Darren McGavin and Julie Sommars

A party of European aristocrats on a hunting trip in New Mexico falls foul of marauding Apaches and the treachery of a guide, who abandons the group and makes off with their possessions. However, a US army scout knows of their presence in the territory and sets out to the rescue. Western, with Sean Connery, Brigitte Bardot, Jack Hawkins, Honor Blackman, Woody Strode, Peter Van Eyck and Eric Sykes

Sherlock Holmes receives a mysterious package with a connection to a series of murders. Aided by his brother Mycroft and trusty sidekick Dr Watson, he is soon on the trail of the Victorian age's most infamous killer - Jack the Ripper. His investigation leads to a conspiracy involving eminent politicians and the aristocracy. Thriller, with John Neville, Donald Houston, John Fraser, Robert Morley, Judi Dench and Barbara Windsor

The heroic sailor pits his wits against an evil magician who has shrunk a princess to the size of a doll - but to break the spell, Sinbad must journey to a mysterious island inhabited by hideous monsters and find a magic lamp. Fantasy adventure, starring Kerwin Mathews, Kathryn Grant and Torin Thatcher, with special effects by Ray Harryhausen
A girl is left to face the world without speech following her experimental upbringing

The Earth is bombarded by what appear to be meteors, but turn out to be the vanguard of an alien invasion force. As America's west coast comes under heavy attack, a platoon of soldiers is sent in to fight off the aliens and rescue civilians - but the troops have only a few hours to complete their mission before the area is bombed. Sci-fi thriller, with Aaron Eckhart and Ramon Rodriguez

A rebellious martial arts expert competes in an underground fighting circuit so he can raise money to save his temple. However, he risks corrupting his spirit as he is drawn further down the path of violence, while the organisers of the arena have their own sinister plans for him. Action adventure, starring Tiger Hu Chen and Keanu Reeves, who also directed. In Cantonese, Mandarin and English

A crooked cop uses his badge and uniform as a cover for his unsavoury money-making schemes and is prepared to murder anyone who stands in his way. A zealous investigator vows to bring him to justice, but the cunning detective responds by turning his adversary's wife against him. Crime thriller, starring Richard Gere, Andy Garcia, Laurie Metcalf, Nancy Travis and William Baldwin

When alcoholic ex-detective Frank Wilson learns of his estranged son's murder, he hits the streets on a crusade for justice, and winds up taking on the mob. Director James Cullen Bressack's thriller, starring DMX, Steven Seagal and Johnny Messner

A secret-service agent wakes up to find himself trapped in the boot of a car. He realises he has been kidnapped by terrorists, who use physical torture as well as more psychological methods to force him to divulge the whereabouts of a safehouse used to protect the US president. Thriller, starring Stephen Dorff, Chyler Leigh and Tom Berenger
Buying goods from the comfort of home
The hero faces a tough battle when he has to stop an Indian medicine man who is on a Hallowe'en killing spree

Laura Hamilton heads to the coastal town of Paralimni in eastern Cyprus to help Yvonne and Tony find their perfect property. Yvonne and Tony first visited Cyprus on their honeymoon 27 years ago and they immediately fell in love with the place. They've been back plenty of times since, but after a few tough years, have decided to seize every second they have and buy a holiday home for the whole family to enjoy. Within their budget of £80,000, Laura shows them five impressive properties

Greg and Tina are searching for a holiday home in western Cyprus, which they plan to share with all their family. Greg has been visiting Cyprus for nearly 40 years, and after introducing Tina to the island, she has fallen in love with it too. Helping them to find the perfect place is property expert Leah Charles-King, who shows them the very best of what their £190,000 budget can buy

Danni Menzies jets off to Portugal's Setúbal Peninsula to help house-hunters Tony and Hendrik from York find their dream holiday home. The couple, who've been married for three years and have two daughters, are looking for somewhere they can all enjoy as a family, for their maximum budget of £330,000

Nick and Rose from Southampton are looking for a holiday home on the Caribbean island of Barbados. Their plan is to spend up to six months a year enjoying the tropical climate and golf facilities. Craig Rowe shows them the best of what their £550,000 budget can get with five impressive properties

Ben Hillman jets off to Portugal's Silver Coast to help mum and daughter Maria and Jess find their dream holiday home. Maria, who is originally from Lisbon, has been living in the UK for almost 40 years but now wants a holiday home that her children and grandchildren can enjoy whenever they like. With a budget of £130,000, Ben shows them five fantastic properties, but will any of them be up Maria and Jess' street?

Danni Menzies heads to Lot-et-Garonne in south-west France to help a Hertfordshire couple find their perfect 'forever' home on a budget of £200,000. Project manager Chris and retired teaching assistant Jane are planning a permanent move to France with their dog Loki, and they're looking for a detached house on the edge of a small village

For Dave and Kelly Elly there's never been another island that compares to Lanzarote. They holidayed there as just friends five years earlier, and now they're married cannot wait to buy a holiday home to enjoy with their families. Scarlette Douglas shows them five properties for their £160,000 budget

Medical insurance boss Zac Kwintner hosts the first dinner party in Gloucestershire, making a traditional Jewish chicken soup, steak fondue and a rich chocolate orange tart. However, handing over cooking duties to his house staff does not go down well with the guests - a mature student, a travel agent, a web designer and a council worker

Mature student Gerry Hill hosts the second party in Gloucestershire, and hopes to spice up the competition with an Egyptian-themed feast. However, his ambitious menu prompts mixed reactions from the guests, and things go from bad to worse when dinner-table banter turns to insults, and one of the diners is forced to go home early

Travel agent Kayleigh Hunt hosts the third dinner party in Gloucestershire, but her Moroccan-themed menu fails to impress the diners when she forgets to cook the main course. With all her guests hungry, she resorts to dressing up in her favourite outfits to keep them entertained

Web designer Marc Harris hosts the penultimate dinner party in Gloucestershire. He is confident his Spanish menu will win over his fellow diners and is determined to put a halt to Zac's rude behaviour, but his plans go downhill when he makes a mess of his starter

Council worker Ameena Cott hosts the final dinner party in Gloucestershire, and hopes to impress with a glamorous evening, which includes colour co-ordinating her dress to match her dog's outfit and making a birdcage centrepiece from a melon. She also tries to win her guests' affections with electric pulse-pad treatment and strawberry face masks, before the winner is announced

The owners of the musically themed Harmony B&B in Torquay, Devon, begin the competition, trying to prove their establishment offers the best value for money. Dutch hosts Hans MacDaniel and Monica van der Meij try to impress their guests, but it remains to be seen what they will make of wheelchair badminton, saxophones at breakfast and a controversial sausage

The contest continues at Chimneys B&B in North Walsham, Norfolk, where owners Jenny and Richard Harmer's decision to use a flag as a tablecloth angers Hans MacDaniel and Monica Van Der Meij. The argument seems to abate during an afternoon canoeing session - only to resurface at breakfast the following day

Beverley Conoley and Caroline Pocklington host at the Wordsworth Hotel in Cockermouth, Cumbria. They take their guests to a spa and Hans MacDaniel happily volunteers for a spray tan, while Richard Harmer is far more uncomfortable as he finds himself on a massage table. The day ends with dinner at a nearby bistro, but Jenny Harmer complains about the temperature

David Attenborough looks at life through the eyes of a newborn elephant calf as he charts the evolution of animal life in the country, and the relationship between nature and the nation's primary religion of Hinduism

Documentary following a team of salvage truck drivers working on Norway's most dangerous roads. A major challenge turns up in the forest

p.t: World's Greatest Train Journeys from Above
p.d: Norway's Bergen line, running from Bergen to Oslo, is filmed from the air as it passes along the fjords of Western Norway, rises to the snowy Hardanger Plateau, and descends through deep forests. Along the way, we learn how a dedicated team of people keep the line open in a challenging environment: clearing snow and ice, deterring wildlife, and repairing damaged trains

p.t: World's Greatest Train Journeys from Above
p.d: This episode follows the luxury El Chepe train from above and on the ground. The route is a wonder of Mexican engineering that took 100 years to build and winds through the world's largest canyon region, Copper Canyon
Investigators seek answers for the families of 298 people killed when an airliner went down over a warzone in eastern Ukraine
Investigators try to solve the mystery of why a brand new design of jet crashed during a demonstration flight

The programme focuses on the tragic events of September 1961, when a Douglas DC-6 operated by Transair Sweden, carrying Dag Hammarskjöld, the second Secretary-General of the United Nations, crashed en route to cease-fire negotiations in Northern Rhodesia during the Congo Crisis.
